cases.excerpt: To address this gap in knowledge, the authors examined the association between circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) and kidney cancer within a large, nested case-control study developed as part of the Cohort Consortium Vitamin D Pooling Project of Rarer Cancers. Concentrations of 25(OH)D were measured from 775 kidney cancer cases and 775 age-, sex-, race-, and season-matched controls from 8 prospective cohort studies.

studies.Population: General population participants of the Copenhagen City Heart Study free of cancer at baseline

sample_size.excerpt: A prospective population-based cohort of 9791 individuals from the Copenhagen City Heart Study who were free of cancer at baseline was followed from 1981-1983 until December 2008 with 100% complete follow-up. During up to 28 years of follow-up, 1081 participants developed a tobacco-related cancer and 1506 developed other cancers.

effect_size.excerpt: Also, multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for a 50% reduction in 25(OH)D were 1.20 (1.13-1.28) for any tobacco-related cancer, 1.19 (95% CI, 1.09-1.31) for lung cancer, 1.44 (1.19-1.73) for head and neck cancer, 1.28 (1.06-1.54) for bladder cancer, 1.34 (1.04-1.73) for kidney cancer, and 0.95 (0.89-1.01) for other cancers. Lower plasma 25(OH)D was associated with higher risk of tobacco-related cancers, but not with risk of other cancers.

studies.Reference: Association of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D with the incidence of 16 cancers, cancer mortality, and all-cause mortality among individuals with metabolic syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
studies.Title: Association of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D with the incidence of 16 cancers, cancer mortality, and all-cause mortality among individuals with metabolic syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
studies.Authors: Wu E, Guo JP, Wang K, Xu HQ, Xie T, Tao L, Ni JT
studies.Timing: median follow-up 10.92 years for cancer incidence outcomes
studies.Population: participants with metabolic syndrome in the UK Biobank cohort

sample_size.excerpt: We enrolled 97,621 participants with MetS at recruitment from the UK Biobank cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: We observed that 25(OH)D concentrations were inversely related to the risk of colon, lung, and kidney cancer, and HRs (95% CI) for 25(OH)D ≥ 75.0 vs. < 25.0 nmol/L were 0.67 (0.45-0.98), 0.64 (0.45-0.91), and 0.54 (0.31-0.95), respectively.

confidence_interval.excerpt: We observed that 25(OH)D concentrations were inversely related to the risk of colon, lung, and kidney cancer, and HRs (95% CI) for 25(OH)D ≥ 75.0 vs. < 25.0 nmol/L were 0.67 (0.45-0.98), 0.64 (0.45-0.91), and 0.54 (0.31-0.95), respectively.

timing.excerpt: Over a median follow-up period of 10.92 years for cancer incidence outcomes

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The exposure factor was baseline serum 25(OH)D concentrations.
